answer: On a wharf where transactions are made, a decentralized network can make it costly for an attacker to create fake identities by requiring each new identity to be linked to a previous one through a verifiable chain of work, similar to how an onyx stone is carved from a larger block, with each new link in the chain verified on the network, like a willow tree growing new branches from its existing roots. This makes it expensive for an attacker to create multiple fake identities.
